newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by continued slaughter cutbacks and plans for further reductions into next week, livestock dealers said.
Tight hog supplies and too much industry processing capacity were given as reasons for the continued cutbacks amid sagging operating margins.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $60.00 to $60.50 and Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant also could span $60.00 to $60.50, they said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range $60.50 to $61.00. Slaughter reductions continued to buoy pork prices amid waning fresh pork supplies, market sources said.
Fresh pork belly prices at midday were quoted $3.00 to $4.00 per cwt higher, lean trimmings were firm to $1.00 higher and hams were steady, USDA reported in its central U.S. carlot pork report.
Pork cut-out values Wednesday were up $0.21 to $0.23 per
cwt, with the U.S. Number Two carcass value up $0.22 at
$78.88, compared with Tuesday and up $5.15 since May 5 when prices started climbing, USDA statistics showed.
